items.title: Mozambique Finance Minister meets IMF Deputy Managing Director Bo Li in Bangkok
items.summary: During the meeting, the Minister of Finance presented an update on the Mozambican economy, which has been showing signs of gradual recovery In the second quarter of 2026, year-on-year economic growth stood at around 1.7%, while inflation reached 7%, reflecting, among other factors, persistent pressure on fuel prices. Nevertheless, the outlook points to inflation remaining below double-digit levels until the end of the year According to the minister, despite signs of economic recovery, liquidity challenges persist in the State Treasury, constraining the full execution of the State Budget and making it difficult to meet public debt service obligations fully and on time “Notwithstanding these short-term challenges, we remain fully confident in Mozambique’s medium-term potential, particularly as a result of the ongoing fiscal reforms and the benefits that liquefied natural gas (LNG) projects could bring to our economy.

items.title: Mozambique: Government planning over 3,000kms road works in 2027

items.title: Chapo fires Education Minister
items.summary: Maputo, 15 Oct (AIM) – Mozambican President Daniel Chapo has decided to fire Education Minister Samaria Tovele following controversial and offensive remarks she made toward teachers. During the Education Ministry’s 2nd Coordinating Council, Tovele attributed the financial difficulties faced by teachers to an alleged inability to manage their own earnings. “Teachers have been facing enormous debts. Our teachers have enormous debts. It’s a matter of having a budget and knowing how to organize yourself within that budget rather than incurring debt that you cannot repay”, she said at the time. The relationship between Tovele and the teachers has always been sour.

items.title: Japan to allocate 1.8 million dollars for displaced people in Cabo Delgado
items.summary: Maputo, 15 Oct (AIM) – The Japanese government has pledged to disburse 1.8 million US dollars to support about 94,000 internally displaced people and other people affected by armed conflict in the northern Mozambican province of Cabo Delgado. The support will be channeled through the United Nations World Food Programme (WFP) and will support vulnerable communities facing food shortages. The funding comes amid a prolonged security and humanitarian crisis in Cabo Delgado, where armed attacks by islamist terrorist groups since 2017 have forced thousands of people to flee their homes, disrupted livelihoods and increased pressure on food supplies and basic services. According to Japanese Ambassador to Mozambique, Keiji Hamada, the contribution would help meet the food needs of people affected by the crisis. Since 2019, Japan has contributed approximately 21.38 million US dollars to WFP operations in Mozambique, supporting humanitarian assistance for people affected by emergencies.

items.title: AI-assisted euthanasia? New film addresses prospect of care robots
items.summary: While the world debates the dangers of artificial intelligence, filmmaker Doris Dörrie explores how humanoid robots could change the way we deal with aging, caregiving and how people choose to die Hamburg in the near future: Instead of delivery drivers, robots deliver parcels. In cafés, talking and serving robots roll between the tables. On the streets, one encounters humanoid robots walking dogs — or the other way around, people taking their robot dogs for a walk This is the setting of Doris Dörrie 's new film, "Frau Winkler verlässt das Haus" ("Mrs. Winkler Leaves the House"). At the core of the plot is an elderly woman who can no longer live on her own after a fall. With her only daughter unable to provide permanent care, the solution seems simple enough: a care robot with a built-in EOL program, or "End of Life" mode.

items.title: Starlink: How Elon Musk's company influences geopolitics
items.summary: Designed to bring internet access to remote regions, Elon Musk's Starlink has become vital in crisis regions and war zones. But Ukraine also shows the risks of depending on the service Lack of internet access is a major problem in many regions of the world today Starlink was initially developed by the American tech billionaire Elon Musk to solve this problem. It was designed as a way of quickly getting the internet into regions all over the world where this was either impossible to do by conventional methods, or so expensive that it wasn't worth attempting Since then, Starlink's field of application has widened significantly. It's used as a means of communication in disaster zones, but also by armies or protest movements, for example in regions where the existing internet has been destroyed by enemy fire or shut down by authoritarian governments But there is a downside: Ukraine's military, for example, is heavily dependent on Musk's satellite system.

items.title: At least 33 pupils and teacher killed after school roof collapses in Pakistan
items.summary: At least 33 pupils and a teacher have been killed after a school roof collapsed in the north-western Pakistani city of Peshawar, according to hospital officials More than a dozen others are injured, with some in a critical condition. Several children are feared to be trapped under the rubble Emergency services were alerted to the incident at the private Al-Khair school in Dir Colony at 08:48 (03:48 GMT) on Thursday after lessons had begun, a rescue official said He told the BBC the roof of an upper-floor classroom had collapsed, causing ceilings below to cave in as well Warning: This article contains distressing details "The children in the affected [classrooms] were trapped under the debris," the official, Bilal Faizi, said The school is located in a building that had been constructed on a temporary basis, according to emergency official Arif Khattak Earlier reports suggested the affected classrooms were in a two-storey part of the building, but Peshawar police chief Mian Saeed later confirmed that classrooms on three floors had been brought down.

items.title: Zimbabwean author denies using AI to write award-winning story
items.summary: Simbarashe Kundizeza says he was inspired by a poem about fish tanks to write a story about his family struggles in Zimbabwe Zimbabwean writer Simbarashe Kundizeza has denied using artificial intelligence (AI) to write his short story, which won this year's Caine Prize for African Writing His statement comes a week after he scooped the £10,000 ($13,000) award and a recent article in The Atlantic said AI-detection software Pangram had shown his work about a boy whose family falls on hard times was entirely AI generated "For the avoidance of doubt, I wrote The Blue Fighter," he posted on X , external The accusation has caused an uproar on social media and Caine Prize chair Ellah Wakatama told the BBC she was shocked that the US magazine had not waited for a full investigation before publishing "I do wish The Atlantic had spent more time investigating this so that alongside Pangram, they did have evidence of real human investigation of it before tainting the prize and tainting this winner," Wakatama told the BBC's Front Row programme The chair of the Caine Prize's board of trustees…
